system_overview: A formal proof module containing TLAPS-checked proofs of the safety properties asserted in the parallel reachability algorithm module. Specifically, it proves that the inductive invariant is maintained by all transitions and that the parallel algorithm implements the safety part (init and next-state relation) of the sequential Misra algorithm under the refinement mapping.
actors_and_components: No new actors. This module extends the parallel reachability algorithm module and the TLAPS proof library to provide machine-checked formal proofs.
state_variables: Inherits all state variables from the parallel reachability algorithm module: the shared marked set, shared frontier, per-process program counters, per-process selected nodes, and per-process successor sets.
safety_properties: Two main results are proved: (1) the invariant (type correctness plus control-flow properties) is preserved by all transitions of the parallel algorithm, and (2) every step of the parallel algorithm corresponds to either a valid step or a stuttering step of the sequential algorithm under the refinement mapping. The proof covers all cases: each process's three actions and the stuttering/termination case.
additional_assumptions: The proofs rely on the assumptions that the root is a valid node and the process set is non-empty and finite. The proofs are structured hierarchically with case analysis over which process and which action is taken. The liveness part of the refinement (fairness) is stated but not proved in this module, as TLAPS does not yet support liveness proofs.
